senses.gloss: sācitta (LP), probably, ‘land attached to government servants as long as they serve’.
Saciva (EI 33; BL; HD), minister or counsellor. See Hist. Dharm., Vol. III, p. 105, note 150.
sa-caur-oddharaṇa (EI 12, 23, 29), ‘together with the right to punish thieves and recover stolen property or fines’; epithet of gift villages. Cf. caura-varja, etc.
